messages.subject: Noisy reactives keep shouting
parts:
I know this has been mentioned a few times, but now it's starting to cause me pain.

Reactives that aren't in the current tab *please* shouldn't fire.  I generally keep drill down views in the back tabs, and since these require 2 orders of magnitude more data to be sent up, I don't want them firing while the user is exploring the front tab.

I had set it up so that reactives with the following roles were wired together:

1) input de-noisers: for instance I want to know if there are 1 input variables or 2.  instead of consuming the input variables I have a reactive which eats both and says 1 or 2
2) database fetchers
3) middleware to clean up the database results
4) graph drawers / data uploaders

I have now started to move the two middle layers to plain old functions, to reduce the chatter that seems to happen even if I don't care about a result right now.

I'm happy to say this seems to work, and reactive inputs consumed by plain functions that are themselves consumed by reactive outputs seems to have the right effect.

But I'm say to see all those funky brackets going.

Note: my app is split into 4 views

1) d3 javascript overview graph (200 json objects with 4 fields)
2) d3 javascript detail graph (2000 json objects with 20 fields)

3) ggplot png version of 1
4) ggplot png version of 2

each of the above also has a co-output which throws a plain data table up beneath the graph.

This means that when all reactives are firing, I'm moving 2 pngs, 2x2000 rows of tables, 2x200 rows of tables, and data for two jsons.

Realistically the user is looking at 2 at once, and would like to press next rapidly to move between records.

BTW: does shiny zlib compress on the wire?

-Alex

Thanks for the lovely tool, btw, I'm going to be using this for lots of stuff.

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Noisy reactives keep shouting
parts:
Thanks for the feedback, Alex!

Winston, Jeff and I have been talking about this kind of stuff recently; we are considering changes to the reactive system to allow entire parts of the reactive graph to be turned off automatically as you tab around. It's pretty tricky to get right (i.e. maintaining correct results!) so it's hard to predict if/when these changes will land in Shiny. However I believe there is some low hanging fruit that will at least make the situation a good deal better.

In the meantime the best workaround I can offer (which you are probably doing) is to give the tabsetPanel an ID, and make sure your output reactives do a check to see if the corresponding tab is active and immediately return NULL if not. You could do this in reactive functions as well if you want, it would help but possibly not as much as you think it would. I would expect a single extra execution for any reactive that is only depended on by outputs that are not visible AND check for whether their tabs are selected at the beginning of their reactive output function. I am hoping to explain why in a blog post over Christmas break (though it is a complicated topic and I am a VERY slow writer, so no promises...).

Shiny isn't currently able to compress on the wire. (Note that it's websocket compression we're talking about, not HTTP, so it's not very widely supported yet on the server side.)
